concern.concern: Proof 1.1 says the face maps are hyperbolic isometries 'because their three corresponding ideal vertices have the same cross-ratio shape.' A triple has no cross-ratio shape, and adjacent tetrahedra need not have equal shapes. The justification is that any bijection between the vertices of two ideal triangular faces extends to their hyperbolic face isometry.

original_concerns.reason: A triple has no cross-ratio shape, and shapes of adjacent tetrahedra may differ. Every ideal triangular face is intrinsically the standard ideal hyperbolic triangle; the assigned vertex bijection determines its unique face isometry. The edge and cusp arguments use that correct fact and need no tetrahedron-shape equality.
